messages:
elaine (OrbitPay): hey team, heads up — at ~10:12 UTC our EU customers started seeing errors and strange outputs. We traced it: requests that usually hit eu-central got routed to us-west and responses look like a smaller model. Some customers report auth token errors and others got billed way more tokens. attaching a minimal repro below.

maria_support: sorry you're hit by this, elaine. can you paste a sample request id + approximate timestamps? also which model you expect? @jun FYI. :eyes:

elaine (OrbitPay): sample req id: req_0a9f3c. request ts: 2101239800. expected model: redwood-pro-1.3 (eu). observed model in responses: redwood-lite-v0.6 (us-west). quick curl we used:

```bash
curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_orbitpay' \n  -H 'X-Region-Preference: eu' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-pro-1.3","input":"Summarize user invoice..."}'
```

and the response snippet we captured:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
model: redwood-lite-v0.6
tokens: 482
warning: tokenizer_mismatch
note: auth_check: OK (token seen valid)
```

jun (eng-runtime): looking at routing logs for req_0a9f3c — appears the eu pool was temporarily exhausted and our routing policy sent traffic to backup pool in us-west. backup pool was running a lite variant (quantized) we use for low-tier capacity. that explains shorter outputs and tokenizer differences.

tom_sre: latency spike at 10:11:55 — autoscaler in eu took ~90s to spin new nodes, fallback routing kicked in at 10:12:00. deploy-bot also shows a capacity reclaim in eu at 10:10.

ops-oncall: @jun can you confirm why fallback pool had incompatible tokenizer/config? we should have variant compatibility guarantees.

jun (eng-runtime): the fallback image was a patch-level build (lite) that uses a different tokenizer.json (vocab indices reordered for quantization). we have a unit test but it only runs for embed pipelines; this slipped through. also routing metadata didn't include model pin for high-tier customers, so policy allowed variant substitution.

sam_billing: billing impact: because tokenizer split tokens differently, token count jumped ~2x for some prompts. that produced unexpected charges for customers during the window (10:12–10:18). we've flagged affected invoices for manual review.

maria_support: for OrbitPay specifically, can we get a timeline + mitigation? customer requests a refund for overbilled calls and wants guaranteed non-substitution moving forward.

jun (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation steps I propose: 1) add model-pinning header honor for enterprise customers so routing won't substitute variants; 2) mark eu pool as priority scale-up and prevent cross-region fallback while scaling; 3) hotfix: sync tokenizer assets across all fallback images. I'll open an engineering ticket.

tom_sre: we've temporarily pinned orbitpay traffic to eu-central and disabled cross-region fallback for accounts with enterprise flag. applied at 10:29 UTC.

deploy-bot: [10:29 UTC] routing-policy update applied: enterprise_no_cross_region_fallback=true (rolled to 100%).

maria_support: noted. elaine, apologized again and we'll file the billing adjustment. can you confirm whether the customer still sees auth errors?

elaine (OrbitPay): auth errors mostly resolved after we pinned traffic. some customers initially had 401s when the swapped model returned unexpected session tokens in headers, but those stopped after 10:32. thanks for the quick response.

jun (eng-runtime): created ENG-1892: "ensure tokenizer parity across fallback variants" and ENG-1893: "support header: enterprise model pinning". putting high priority on ENG-1892.

sam_billing: created BILL-4567 for manual invoice adjustments for OrbitPay and a batch job to detect similar spikes.

ops-oncall: follow-ups: run a resume incident postmortem, add a canary for tokenizer checksum mismatch on rollout, and include route pinning as a feature for high-tier customers. assigning to tom_sre + jun.

maria_support: I'll send OrbitPay a timeline + credit note and keep thread posted. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
